title: Voxel-based 3D Facies Segmentation from Seismic Data: A Comparative Study
abstract: arXiv:2608.14058v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Seismic facies segmentation has emerged as a significant challenge in geophysics, requiring robust methods and systems to effectively identify geologically analogous facies with limited labeled data. Although existing studies have shown promising results in 2D facies segmentation, they often preprocess the original 3D seismic volumes into sets of 2D slices, typically the inline and crossline directions, and treat this problem as a purely 2D segmentation task. This simplification introduces discontinuities across slices and fails to preserve the spatial and structural continuity in 3D seismic data, thus limiting the model's ability to learn coherent geological patterns. In this work, we present a comparative and reproducible benchmark for voxel-based 3D seismic facies segmentation, built upon publicly available seismic volumes including the Netherlands F3 and the Parihaka datasets, with standardized data splits and evaluation metrics. translated_title: 基于体素的3D地震数据相分割：一项比较研究
translated_abstract: 摘要：地震相分割已成为地球物理学中的一个重大挑战，需要稳健的方法和系统，以便在有限标注数据的情况下有效识别地质上相似的相。尽管现有研究在2D相分割方面显示出有前景的结果，但它们通常将原始3D地震体预处理为2D切片集（通常是沿线和交叉线方向），并将此问题视为纯2D分割任务。这种简化引入了切片之间的不连续性，未能保留3D地震数据中的空间和结构连续性，从而限制了模型学习连贯地质模式的能力。在本工作中，我们构建了一个基于体素的3D地震相分割的比较性、可复现基准，基于公开可用的地震体（包括荷兰F3和Parihaka数据集），并采用标准化的数据划分和评估指标。
tldr: 本研究提出了首个基于体素的3D地震相分割比较基准，利用公开数据集和标准化评估，以克服传统2D方法中空间连续性的丢失问题。
en_tdlr: This work introduces the first voxel-based 3D seismic facies segmentation benchmark, leveraging public datasets and standardized evaluation to address the loss of spatial continuity in conventional 2D approaches.
